negative_subtype_replication: PARTIAL -- negatives-not-separated-from-each-other replicates; positives-score-higher-than-negatives does NOT replicate OOS
what_this_study_establishes: Stage-1 broad flip prediction remains valid and reproducible (frozen Model C in-sample: LONG ROC=0.6754, SHORT ROC=0.6768; deterministic refit parity confirmed, corr>=0.997 all arms).
P90-upcross conditioning compresses Stage-1 score variance ~4x (std 0.11->0.026 LONG, 0.107->0.027 SHORT).
Most of the Stage-1 ~0.67 -> Stage-2 ~0.5 AUC reduction is explained by range restriction from high-score conditioning (population effect: LONG -0.152, SHORT -0.138 ROC), not a modeling defect.
Changing the label from flip-only to T1 (flip AND MFE>=1atr AND MAE<=0.5atr) adds a smaller secondary reduction (LONG -0.006, SHORT -0.028 ROC).

The tested Stage-2 causal feature sets (Arms A/B/C, 21 predeclared inputs) do not robustly identify clean/tradable reversals among high-confidence Stage-1 upcrosses -- TRAIN's LONG B signal collapses OOS; SHORT A is weak and not cleanly calibrated.
This study does NOT establish that no feature in the full 129-feature canonical registry could ever help -- it only rejects the predeclared 21-input A/B/C universe actually tested.
